content.overview: BNS s. 264 — Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for. BNS restatement of IPC 228. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 228. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 264 is the rule on “Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for”. The section provides that whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to apprehend, or to keep in confinement, any person in any case not provided for in section 259, section 260 or section 261, or in any other law for the time being in force, omits to apprehend that person or suffers him to escape from confinement, shall be punished—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 264 exists so that “Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

The provision in detail
264. Whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to apprehend, or to keep in confinement, any person in any case not provided for in section 259, section 260 or section 261, or in any other law for the time being in force, omits to apprehend that person or suffers him to escape from confinement, shall be punished—

(a) if he does so intentionally, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and

(b) if he does so negligently, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both

Essential ingredients

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 264 (Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for), Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to apprehend, or to keep in confinement, any person in any case not provided for in section 259, section 260 or section 261, or in any other law for the time being in force, omits to apprehend that person or suffers him to escape from confinement, shall be punished—

Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 264 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 264 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
